items.title: Chico Hamilton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 30, 2000
items.q: I spent about fifteen years playing for singers, nothing but singers. And I was with Lena Horne for eight years.

ctx.x: Funny to talk about it now.

You could just imagine seeing that you know? And I’ve had a lot of beautiful experiences playing with various — I think the most rewarding in a sense, experience that I’ve had, I spent about fifteen years playing for singers, nothing but singers. And I was with Lena Horne for eight years. And during that period with Lena Horne it took me out of the realm of just being a musician. It took me into show biz. That’s a big difference between a musician, a jazz musician, and show biz people, the whole thing. It just…
It’s not as easy as it sounds.

items.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: And I was with her for eight years.

ctx.x: Her husband. Man, my life turned completely around. Being a street urchin, I was introduced for the first time to show biz, which I knew nothing about on that level, on that scale, you know. And my whole life turned around, man. And I was with her for eight years. Her husband & Luther -- and then he taught me how to play chess, taught me how to eat lobster, taught me how to drink cognac, all that, you know. It was dynamite, man. All of a sudden man, it was like I was on a first name basis with everybody from…
Ella was a piece of cake. Incidentally man, I made my first record with Ella, with (Unintelligible)(Slim?) and Slam . That was way back in -­
